source_name: the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DLI) Construction Codes and Licensing Division public license registry
methodology_source_html:
Source

Every listing is extracted from the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DLI) — Construction Codes and Licensing Division — public license registry file for the electrical program (MNDLILicRegCertExport_Electrical.csv, published at secure.doli.state.mn.us/ccld/data/), pulled on {as_of}. The file covers {rows} rows. Listed license classes:

Electrical Contractor (Class A / Class B) — the business license to sell and perform electrical work; Master Electrician (Class A / B) and Journeyworker Electrician (Class A / B) — individual credentials; Maintenance Electrician — a limited individual credential.

Excluded on purpose (and why): registered unlicensed electricians —the largest row group in the file—by definition hold no electrician license and are not presented here as electricians; power-limited technicians and technology-systems contractors (the low-voltage trade, a different license family); satellite / sign installers; linemen (utility trade); and registered electrical employers (an employer registration, not a worker license). Statuses treated as inactive: expired, revoked, suspended, and voluntary terminations — none are listed.
methodology_inclusion_extra_html: • Personal licenses (journeyworker / master) without a business or DBA name are listed as solo operators at the address on file. Licenses whose city field cannot be resolved to a Minnesota municipality (~{dropped_no_city} rows, including entries with malformed registry addresses) are excluded from city listings; the DLI lookup remains the verification source of record.
ordering_html:
• License class held: contractor licenses first, then master electricians, then journeyworker / maintenance.
  • Registry tenure — earlier first issuance ranks first (shown on each listing as “licensed since”).
  • Clean registry record — licenses flagged with an enforcement action rank below unflagged ones, and every flagged listing discloses that flag.
  • Number of active licenses held at that address.
  • Telephone number on file (contactable businesses first).
  • Alphabetical by name — deterministic.
